Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 1, Verse 46

“If the armed sons of Dhritarashtra should kill me in battle, unresisting and unarmed, that would be better for me.”

The furthest point his reasoning can reach: he would rather be killed than kill. It is not cowardice — he is choosing the one outcome in which nobody pays but him.
